name: AZHottie · Complete Model Interview
description: The original editable 68-question interview: 36 multiple-choice and 32 open-ended prompts. Questions 25–36 are private casting questions.

questions.text: You are fully dressed on a boudoir set. The direction is "more sexual tension." What do you change first?
choices: Keep the clothes; let the eye contact do the undressing.
Take command of the frame with stronger posture and deliberate movement.
Play the tease: a knowing smile, then a perfectly composed expression.
Ask for a visual reference and build the tension through light, styling, and framing.

questions.text: AZHottie proposes an editorial called "Nothing to Hide." Which interpretation would you pitch?
choices: An artistic nude portrait with direct eye contact and a restrained composition.
A nude silhouette where lighting shapes the final image.
Implied nudity with carefully arranged fabric and agreed coverage.
Lingerie and an expression that says the subject is entirely in control.
A fully clothed portrait where the title refers to an unapologetic personality.

questions.text: The lingerie shoot looks beautiful but too polite. The photographer asks for "a little bad intention." What is your approach?
choices: Replace the friendly smile with a direct, challenging expression.
Bring a wicked sense of humor to the pose and delivery.
Play a glamorous character who knows exactly why everyone is looking.
Ask what story the character is telling, then perform that intention.

questions.text: You have agreed to an artistic nude shoot, but the first frame feels anonymous. How would you make it recognizably yours?
choices: Put expression and personality at the center of the portrait.
Use a strong pose and distinctive styling elements.
Add a playful detail that breaks the solemn mood.
Work with the photographer on a composition that reflects my own idea of confidence.

questions.text: A very sensual take ends with you laughing. What would you propose?
choices: Shoot a second take that keeps a trace of the laughter; confidence can have a sense of humor.
Reset and deliver the polished version we planned.
Create two finished versions: serious editorial and mischievous character.
Save the candid moment for a separately approved behind-the-scenes feature.

questions.text: In the public interview, the host asks, "What makes a photograph erotic to you?" Which answer is closest?
choices: The subject looks as though they chose every part of being seen.
The expression creates a question the image does not completely answer.
Confidence, intention, and the relationship between the subject and the camera.
The complete composition: styling, light, pose, and mood working together.

questions.text: During Tanning Lessons, an ordinary poolside demonstration becomes a ridiculously serious class. How do you escalate the joke?
choices: Teach advanced tan-line geometry as though my academic reputation depends on it.
Judge posing technique with scandalously intense authority.
Play the deadpan assistant whose reactions expose the instructor's vanity.
Turn every instruction into an opportunity for my character's personal photo shoot.

questions.text: In the scripted Wet T-Shirt Team Tryouts sketch, the host announces the most important audition in Arizona. What performance do you bring?
choices: A contestant treating the absurd audition like a career-defining runway appearance.
A judge demanding an artistic explanation for every pose.
A host reporting every minor development as a major scandal.
An unimpressed contestant whose dry commentary steals the scene.

questions.text: You and another adult model are creating a lingerie campaign. Which performance dynamic would you suggest?
choices: Two equally confident leads sharing the frame.
A composed lead and a mischievous partner, switching roles between takes.
Playful rivals whose competition is clearly part of the character work.
Two distinct individual portraits followed by a carefully planned joint image.

questions.text: A scripted scene calls for flirtatious chemistry with another model. What would help you make it convincing?
choices: Rehearse the banter until the timing feels effortless.
Agree on movement and any contact, then leave room for expression within that plan.
Build contrasting characters so the attraction is communicated through the performance.
Use clear direction and camera framing to create the scene's tension.

questions.text: Your cohost delivers a suggestive joke and looks to you for the next beat. How do you respond?
choices: Deliver the next practical fact with a completely straight face.
Give one raised eyebrow, sharpen the joke, and return to the scene.
Ask an innocent-sounding question that makes their exaggeration the punchline.
Switch roles so they become the composed expert and I take over the mischief.

questions.text: Your scene partner keeps breaking character during a supposedly seductive commercial. How would you handle the next take?
choices: Use the laughter as part of the character and pitch a comedy version.
Rehearse the difficult beat privately, then return to the original performance.
Swap roles and see whether the new dynamic works better.
Record the polished version first and save an approved comedy take for afterward.

questions.text: The Strip Tease trailer must make the title memorable before gameplay is revealed. What is your approach?
choices: A composed introduction that acknowledges the title and lets the pause do the work.
A mischievous host who clearly enjoys the audience's assumptions.
A glamorous promotional portrait brought to life through expression and movement.
Deadpan delivery, treating the provocative title like the most ordinary announcement imaginable.

questions.text: You and another model are hosting a Strip Tease game demonstration. Once the actual rules are supplied, how would you divide the performance?
choices: I explain the confirmed steps while my cohost demonstrates and reacts.
My cohost teaches; I play the flirtatiously overconfident newcomer who still needs instructions.
We alternate demonstrations and give each other dry commentary.
We make a clear tutorial, then a separate comedy version using the same accurate rules.

questions.text: During the Strip Tease interview, the host asks, "Are you here to teach the game or be a distraction?" How do you play the moment?
choices: "I can explain the rules and still be your favorite complication." Then give a clear explanation.
"Watch the game. I'll know if you're not." Then hand the demonstration to my cohost.
Invite the cohost to teach while I react as the exaggeratedly confident newcomer.
Deliver a dry look, point to the game, and let the edit land the joke.

questions.text: A sex toy is on the demonstration table. How do you open the video?
choices: Name it plainly, pick it up, and walk viewers through the visible controls.
"Yes, it's a sex toy. We can all stop whispering." Then explain the features.
Start with product close-ups while I narrate what each control does.
Ask my cohost what a buyer would want to know, then demonstrate those features.

questions.text: Your cohost looks glamorous holding the product but cannot find the right button. What do you do?
choices: Stay in character and point out the correct control while the awkward pause earns the laugh.
Turn it into a quick demonstration of what that button actually does.
Keep the moment for an approved blooper, then record a polished take together.
Let my cohost play the frustrated expert while I read the instructions with absurd seriousness.

questions.text: The adult product demonstration is accurate but sounds embarrassed. How would you improve it?
choices: Name the product directly and explain its features with calm confidence.
Open with one unapologetic joke, then get straight to the useful details.
Make the reluctance to name the product the joke, then present it plainly.
Use elegant product close-ups and a direct, assured voice-over.

questions.text: Two performers, a boudoir set, and an adult product: which campaign would you pitch?
choices: An editorial portrait in agreed wardrobe followed by a confident product introduction.
A lavish commercial that resembles a perfume launch, then reveals exactly what we are advertising.
A polished presenter explaining the product while a deadpan partner critiques the excessive glamour.
Two contrasting takes, one elegantly serious and one openly mischievous, for an audience comparison.

questions.text: The candy campaign wants unmistakable innuendo. What would you shoot?
choices: A luxurious unwrapping sequence with "The wrapper is the first thing to go" delivered to camera.
Two hosts debating scandalous candy names as though negotiating an extremely serious business deal.
Beautiful product close-ups with shameless double meanings delivered in a calm voice.
A mock gift consultation matching cheekily named candies to fictional occasions and personalities.

questions.text: A revealing outfit needs a campaign with personality. What would you contribute?
choices: A confident editorial performance where expression is as memorable as the clothing.
A playful styling demonstration that shows how I'd actually wear it.
A mock-serious fashion review with a cohost who keeps making suggestive observations.
Two character versions of the same look: polished glamour and troublemaker.

questions.text: The fitness campaign needs useful demonstrations and AZHottie attitude. What is your role?
choices: Demonstrate movements within my experience with confident, direct delivery.
Model the apparel while a knowledgeable cohost explains the exercise or equipment.
Play the flirtatiously overconfident character who discovers the warm-up is actual work.
Host a playful team challenge while keeping the demonstration clear.

questions.text: A spa campaign asks for adult glamour and a sense of humor. What concept would you choose?
choices: A beautifully styled guest who is completely unapologetic about being pampered.
A professional relaxer treating a day of self-care like a demanding executive appointment.
Two models delivering dry commentary about the ambitious work of doing absolutely nothing.
An elegant tour of the actual services with a candid, personable host.

questions.text: You can lead one recurring AZHottie project. Which would you choose?
choices: An erotic editorial series exploring different visual concepts and team personalities.
Adult product introductions with candid explanations and a witty cohost.
Strip Tease demonstrations and comedy built around the team's personalities.
Boudoir, fashion, fitness, or spa campaigns connected by behind-the-scenes stories.
A recurring comedy series featuring Tanning Lessons, tryouts, and product parodies.

questions.text: Which kinds of work would you like to discuss?
choices: Erotic or boudoir editorial photography.
Comedy, hosting, and scripted flirtation.
Clothing, fitness, candy, or spa campaigns.
Adult product photography and presentations.
Strip Tease promotional work or game-related creative contributions.
I'd like to review specific opportunities before choosing.

questions.text: Which exposure levels are you open to discussing for a defined shoot?
choices: Clothed fashion, fitness, or swimwear.
Lingerie or underwear.
Implied nudity with agreed coverage.
Topless photography.
Full artistic or editorial nudity.
I'd prefer to discuss this privately before selecting any level.

questions.text: Which forms of collaboration would you consider?
choices: Joint images or cohosting without physical contact.
Scripted flirtation and suggestive banter.
Close posing with specifically agreed contact.
A scripted kiss with another adult performer, agreed individually for the scene.
Solo work only.

questions.text: If Strip Tease used a performer's image, voice, or likeness, what would you want to discuss?
choices: Hosting or voice work.
Promotional photography or video.
Use within the game after reviewing the actual scenes, presentation, and terms.
Writing, design, or production contributions.
I'd prefer another project.

questions.text: Which adult product demonstration formats would you consider?
choices: Displaying products or packaging.
Showing controls and features at a tabletop demonstration station.
Presenting factual product information on camera.
Styled campaign photographs with agreed wardrobe and products.
Voice-over, writing, filming, or editing.
Adult product demonstrations are not for me.

questions.text: How would you prefer to be identified in adult-themed work?
choices: My face visible with the professional name I already use publicly.
My face visible with a stage name chosen for this work.
My face visible without a credited name.
My face concealed without a credited name.
I'd decide after reviewing the publication plan.

questions.text: Which public interview arrangement would you consider?
choices: An interview limited to questions and topics agreed in advance.
An edited feature in which I approve the selected personal answers before publication.
Audio or written answers with a separately agreed name and image presentation.
I'd prefer to keep all interview answers private for now.

questions.text: What behind-the-scenes participation would you consider?
choices: Planned segments with an agreed brief.
Candid material I review before publication.
Scheduled interviews and production updates only.
Occasional appearances agreed individually.
The finished performance only.

questions.text: Which details would you want to discuss before a daring project?
choices: Concept, wardrobe, exposure, and camera angles.
Who will be present and any interaction with other performers.
Where the material will appear and how my identity will be used.
Payment, time, travel, and deliverables.
Review arrangements and how to pause or change the agreed scene.
All of the above.

questions.text: What participation schedule could you realistically consider?
choices: Occasional projects, around once or twice a month.
A regular weekly production block.
Several production blocks per week.
Short runs of dates for specific campaigns.
I'd need to review the dates and location for each project.

questions.text: Which paid working arrangements would you consider?
choices: A defined fee for each shoot or appearance.
An ongoing paid role with an agreed schedule.
A base fee plus a clearly defined commission or bonus.
Separate fees for performance and creative production.
I'd need the scope and usage terms before discussing rates.

questions.text: What would you most want to contribute as the team builds AZHottie?
choices: A recognizable modeling and performance presence.
Hosting, comedy, or a recurring character.
Creative concepts, scripts, styling, or production.
Product ideas, demonstrations, and campaign development.
Agreed promotion through my own channels.
I'd like to start with one project and see where I fit.

questions.text: What is one on-camera fantasy you'd love to turn into an AZHottie shoot, performance, or story?
What is the most daring or risqué video you've made, and what made it feel daring to you?
Have you ever kissed an adult woman? If you're comfortable sharing, was it on camera or a personal moment?
Describe a time you felt especially confident, sexy, or uninhibited in front of a camera. What helped you get there?
Have you ever shared unexpected on-camera chemistry with another adult performer? What made the collaboration work?
What is the most provocative AZHottie concept you'd want to pitch: a shoot, sketch, game promotion, or product campaign?
Which adult product or topic could you discuss on camera more candidly than most people, and why?
What would you want a director or scene partner to understand about you before creating something daring together?
Have you ever posted a revealing photo for exactly one person's attention and pretended it was for everyone? Did they take the hint?
What is the most innocent caption you've attached to a revealing photo when your real intention was anything but innocent?
Have you ever sent a suggestive photo and spent more time checking for a reply than you spent taking it?
What is the most calculated flirtation you've successfully passed off as an accident?
Tell us about a time "we're just friends" wasn't the whole truth.
What is the most scandalous assumption someone has made about you that was completely wrong, and one they got embarrassingly right?
Have you ever gone skinny-dipping with other adults? Whose idea was it, and how quickly did you agree?
What would be harder to admit publicly: that you deliberately invited the attention, that you enjoyed it more than expected, or that one particular adult's reaction mattered most? Why?
Which boudoir photograph of you would most surprise someone who thinks you're innocent, and what would you enjoy about their reaction?
Have you ever asked, "Is this photo too much?" while secretly hoping someone would encourage you to publish it? What was your real hesitation?
What is the boldest photo of yourself you've chosen to keep private, and what has kept it private?
When have you been least convincing while insisting that your chemistry with another adult performer was "just acting"?
Have you ever kept a flirtatious character going after "cut" because the mutual chemistry was too enjoyable to drop? How did you acknowledge it?
If you chose to shoot nude, what would make you more nervous: posing, seeing the finished pictures, or showing someone whose opinion matters to you? Why?
Which would you be more tempted to keep private: the revealing photo or the message you sent with it? Why?
Have you ever acted scandalized by an adult-themed shoot idea while secretly wanting to be part of it? What was holding you back?
